name: Montane / cloud forest
notes: Persistently fog-soaked montane forest of low, gnarled, moss-laden trees with bamboo thickets, tree ferns and a heavy epiphyte load of bromeliads, orchids and liverworts; drawn on the Andes, Central America and the Afromontane belt.

canopy.name: Gnarled cloud-forest tree
canopy.source: Weinmannia tomentosa, encenillo, northern Andes (Colombia/Venezuela) cloud forest 2400-3400 m, twisted moss-covered trunks 8-20 m — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

canopy.name: Cloud-forest oak
canopy.source: Quercus costaricensis, Talamanca cloud-forest oak, Costa Rica/Panama 2000-3300 m, dominant 20-35 m with bromeliad-laden limbs — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

canopy.name: Podocarp
canopy.source: Podocarpus oleifolius, Andean podocarp, Mexico to Bolivia montane cloud forest 1500-3500 m, 15-30 m — Wikipedia / Gymnosperm Database

canopy.name: Clusia
canopy.source: Clusia multiflora, gaque, northern Andes cloud forest 1500-3200 m, thick leathery leaves, stilt roots, 8-20 m — Kew POWO / Wikipedia

canopy.name: Hagenia
canopy.source: Hagenia abyssinica, African redwood, Afromontane cloud forest 2400-3600 m (Ethiopia-Malawi), spreading crown 10-20 m, red flower panicles — Wikipedia / PROTA

shrub.name: Mountain bamboo
shrub.source: Yushania alpina, African alpine bamboo, Afromontane belt 2400-3300 m (Kenya, Uganda, Ethiopia, Rwanda), dense stands 6-15 m — Wikipedia / PROTA

shrub.name: Andean chusquea
shrub.source: Chusquea scandens, chusque, northern Andes cloud forest 1800-3500 m, scrambling clump bamboo 3-8 m — Kew POWO / Wikipedia

shrub.name: Andean tree fern
shrub.source: Cyathea caracasana, Andean tree fern, Central America to Bolivia cloud forest 1000-3000 m, trunk 4-12 m — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

shrub.name: Andean miconia
shrub.source: Miconia theizans, melastome shrub, Neotropical montane forest 1000-3000 m, common gap coloniser 2-6 m — Kew POWO / Tropicos

shrub.name: Fuchsia
shrub.source: Fuchsia boliviana, Bolivian fuchsia, Andes of Peru/Bolivia/Argentina cloud forest 1000-3000 m, 2-4 m, hanging red flowers — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

ground.name: Moss carpet
ground.source: Thuidium delicatulum, delicate fern moss, cosmopolitan, forms dense carpets on cloud-forest floor and logs, 3-10 cm — Wikipedia / Tropicos

ground.name: Filmy fern
ground.source: Hymenophyllum polyanthos, filmy fern, pantropical montane cloud forest, translucent one-cell-thick fronds 5-20 cm on rocks, logs and trunks — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

ground.name: Hard fern
ground.source: Blechnum occidentale, hammock fern, Neotropics lowland to montane forest, 30-60 cm fronds, red-tinged new growth — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

ground.name: Begonia
ground.source: Begonia foliosa, fern-leaf begonia, northern Andes cloud forest 1500-3000 m, shaded banks, 20-60 cm, pink flowers — Kew POWO / Wikipedia

ground.name: Peperomia
ground.source: Peperomia galioides, Andean peperomia, Mexico to Bolivia montane forest 1000-3500 m, succulent whorled leaves 10-40 cm — Kew POWO / Tropicos

epiphyte.name: Epiphytic moss and liverworts
epiphyte.source: Plagiochila bifaria, leafy liverwort, pantropical and oceanic cloud forests, hangs in dense mats from branches with mosses, 5-30 cm — Wikipedia / Tropicos

epiphyte.name: Tank bromeliad
epiphyte.source: Guzmania monostachia, West Indian tufted airplant, Florida & Neotropics to Andes 0-2500 m, epiphytic water-tank rosette 30-60 cm, red-tipped spike — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

epiphyte.name: Epidendrum orchid
epiphyte.source: Epidendrum secundum, crucifix orchid, Andes and Central America 800-3400 m, epiphytic or on mossy banks, 30-100 cm, pink-orange flowers — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

epiphyte.name: Beard lichen
epiphyte.source: Usnea barbata, beard lichen, cosmopolitan in humid montane forest, pale grey-green tufts hanging from twigs 10-50 cm — Wikipedia

special.note: Catalogue plants (data/plants) whose band centres fall inside this biome's climate; computed, informational. Phase 6 may raise their density here so they are findable.

associations.name: Andean upper montane cloud forest
associations.where: steep mid-slopes in the persistent fog belt, wet
associations.source: Gentry 1995 in Hamilton et al. Tropical Montane Cloud Forests; Grubb 1977

associations.name: Oak-podocarp cloud forest
associations.where: high ridges and slopes of Central America, fog-soaked
associations.source: Kappelle 1996 Los Bosques de Roble de la Cordillera de Talamanca; Hamilton et al. 1995

associations.name: Hagenia Afromontane forest
associations.where: upper slopes of the East African volcanoes, moist
associations.source: Hedberg 1951 Vegetation belts of the East African mountains

associations.name: Montane bamboo thicket
associations.where: landslide scars, ridge crests and gaps after disturbance
associations.source: Hedberg 1951 (bamboo zone); Young 1991 Chusquea in the Andes

associations.name: Elfin mossy ridge forest
associations.where: windswept ridge tops and summits, waterlogged thin soil
associations.source: Grubb 1977 Control of forest growth on wet tropical mountains; Bruijnzeel et al. 2011
